scope: NCERT Class XI Biology, Chapter 8: Cell — The Unit of Life

cases.question: Which cell organelle is the principal site of aerobic respiration and cellular ATP production?

allowedMisconceptions.description: The learner assumes the organelle that controls cellular activity physically performs every major cellular process.
The learner partially remembers the term powerhouse but cannot connect it to ATP production.
The transcript does not support a safe diagnosis.

verifiedFacts: The nucleus contains genetic material and regulates cellular activities.
Mitochondria are sites of aerobic respiration.
Mitochondria produce cellular energy as ATP.
The inner mitochondrial membrane forms cristae.

transferQuestion.question: A cell has a very high and continuous demand for ATP. Which organelle would you expect to be especially abundant?

recallCard.front: Control centre vs energy-production site: which organelle does each job?
recallCard.back: Nucleus regulates cellular activity; mitochondria perform aerobic respiration and produce ATP.

cases.spokenRepair: Nucleus cell ka control centre hai, lekin control karna aur process ka actual site hona alag baat hai. Aerobic respiration aur ATP production mitochondria mein hoti hai.
cases.clarifyingQuestion: Kya tumhe laga control centre har process khud karta hai, ya 'powerhouse' term yaad tha but ATP link miss hua?

cases.question: Which statement best describes osmosis across a cell membrane?

options.text: Movement of any solute from high concentration to low concentration
Diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane
Movement of ions against a concentration gradient using ATP

allowedMisconceptions.description: The learner treats every high-to-low movement as osmosis.
The learner remembers water movement but omits the selectively permeable membrane condition.
The transcript does not support a safe diagnosis.

verifiedFacts: Passive transport does not require energy.
Neutral solutes can move by simple diffusion along a concentration gradient.
Movement of water by diffusion across a membrane is called osmosis.
Active transport moves substances against a concentration gradient and uses ATP.

transferQuestion.question: A membrane allows water to pass but not sugar. Water moves toward the side with the higher sugar concentration. Which process is occurring?

recallCard.front: What makes osmosis different from ordinary diffusion?
recallCard.back: Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane.

cases.spokenRepair: High se low movement diffusion ka general idea hai. Osmosis specifically water ka diffusion hai, aur selectively permeable membrane ke across hota hai.
cases.clarifyingQuestion: Kya tum har high-to-low movement ko osmosis keh rahi thi, ya water yaad tha but selective membrane condition miss hui?

cases.question: Which cellular structure directly translates mRNA into protein?

allowedMisconceptions.description: The learner assumes that because Golgi handles proteins, it is the structure that creates them.
The learner cannot distinguish production from modification, sorting, and packaging.
The transcript does not support a safe diagnosis.

verifiedFacts: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.
The Golgi apparatus packages material for delivery or secretion.
Some proteins synthesized on ER-associated ribosomes are modified in the Golgi.

transferQuestion.question: A newly formed secretory protein is being produced from an mRNA template. Which structure performs the production step?

recallCard.front: Ribosome and Golgi: what is the key difference?
recallCard.back: Ribosome synthesizes protein; Golgi modifies, sorts, and packages material.

cases.spokenRepair: Golgi proteins ko modify, sort aur package karta hai. Protein synthesis ka actual step ribosome karta hai by translating mRNA.
cases.clarifyingQuestion: Kya tumhe laga protein ko handle karna hi protein banana hai, ya ribosome–ER–Golgi sequence confuse hua?

cases.question: Which process moves ions against their concentration gradient using cellular energy?

allowedMisconceptions.description: The learner classifies any particle movement as diffusion.
The learner ignores whether movement is down or against the concentration gradient.
The learner misses the significance of ATP use.
The transcript does not support a safe diagnosis.

verifiedFacts: Passive transport does not require energy.
Simple diffusion proceeds along a concentration gradient.
Active transport moves substances against a concentration gradient.

transferQuestion.question: A membrane pump moves an ion from a region of lower concentration to a region of higher concentration. What must be true?

recallCard.front: What two clues identify active transport?
recallCard.back: Movement against the concentration gradient and use of cellular energy, usually ATP.

cases.spokenRepair: Passive transport gradient ke saath hota hai aur energy nahi leta. Active transport gradient ke against hota hai aur ATP use karta hai.
cases.clarifyingQuestion: Kya tumne har particle movement ko diffusion maana, ya gradient direction aur ATP clue miss hua?
